question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}48y(x-y),\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{x}{2}, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{4}{5},$ $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{1}{4},$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=\frac{2}{3},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2},
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

First, we find $\text{Var}[X].$ Using the given results, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}-{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{75}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x/2}{y}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x/2}48{y}^{3}(x-y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =48{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x/2}(x{y}^{3}-{y}^{4})\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =48{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}-\frac{1}{5}{y}^{5}]}_{y=0}^{y=x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =48{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{64}{x}^{5}-\frac{1}{160}{x}^{5})\text{d}x \\  & =48\cdot \frac{3}{320}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{5}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{9}{20}{[\frac{1}{6}{x}^{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{40}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{40}-{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{80}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's find $\text{Cov}[X,Y].$ By the rule of the lazy statistician, we find $\text{E}[XY]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x/2}xy\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x/2}48x{y}^{2}(x-y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =48{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x/2}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}-x{y}^{3})\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & =48{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =48{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{24}{x}^{5}-\frac{1}{64}{x}^{5})\text{d}x \\  & =48\cdot \frac{5}{192}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{5}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{4}{[\frac{1}{6}{x}^{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{5}{24}-(\frac{4}{5})\cdot (\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{120}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{75} & \frac{1}{120} \\ \frac{1}{120} & \frac{1}{80}\end{aligned}].
$$
